papers.title: Gauss' law for arbitrarily moving Gaussian surfaces: A revisit
papers.abstract: We have re-examined the integral form of Gauss' law for arbitrarily moving charges inside and outside an arbitrarily expanding (or contracting) and deforming Gaussian surface. We have explicitly calculated the time-dependent Gauss' flux integral for such a generic non-static case with the Maxwell equations under consideration. We have obtained an evolution equation $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\text{t}}\oint_{s(t)}\vec{E}\cdot\text{d}\vec{s}(t)=\frac{I^{(s)}_{\text{in}}(t)}{\epsilon_0}$ for the time-dependence of the flux-integral. We have demonstrated pedagogically that while the flux integral is dependent on the expansion/contraction of the surface, it is independent of its deformation.
